saints.name: St. John of Kanty
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Polish priest and professor of Kraków, famed for learning matched by humility and boundless charity to the poor…
biography: John was born at Kęty, near Oświęcim in the diocese of Kraków, about 1390, the son of devout country folk, Stanislaus and Anne. Sent to the Academy of Kraków, he took degrees in philosophy and theology, was ordained priest, and became a beloved professor of the university.

He served briefly as parish priest at Olkusz, but, shrinking from the burden of souls, soon returned to Kraków to the chair of Sacred Scripture, which he held until his death. His austerity was proverbial: he slept little and on the floor, ate sparingly, abstained from meat, and gave the poor all he had beyond bare need.

He made four pilgrimages to Rome on foot and one to Jerusalem, desiring, it was said, martyrdom among the Turks. On his manuscripts he wrote a warning against strife and slander: 'Conturbare cave: non est placare suave; infamare cave: nam revocare grave' — avoid contention; avoid slander, which cannot be recalled.

He died at Kraków on Christmas Eve, 1473, and was buried beneath the church of St. Anne, where his tomb grew famed for miracles. Canonized by Pope Clement XIII in 1767, he is venerated as a patron of Poland and of teachers and students.
saints.knownFor: A learned and charitable priest, patron of Poland and of scholars.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 October
